neighbours.label: A less common word or name starting with Y after a space, e.g. Yahweh, Yemen, Yosemite, Yin, yak, yaw, yoga, yard, yogurt; the everyday words you, your, year, young, yes, yet stay low, as does y inside a word (Tokyo, kayak) or Y at the very start of the text
fire: The hikers spent three days camping in Yosemite before heading home.
She ordered a bowl of yogurt topped with fresh berries.
A shaggy yak carried the supplies up the steep mountain trail.
The pilot corrected the yaw as the plane drifted in the crosswind.
Every morning he unrolls his mat and practices yoga for an hour.
The kids played soccer in the back yard until it got dark.
The ancient text refers to the deity by the name Yahweh.
Fighting continued along the coast of Yemen last month.
quiet: Have you ever spent three days camping in the mountains?
She ordered a bowl of oatmeal topped with fresh berries, as she does every year.
Our guide paddled a kayak across the cold mountain lake.
The pilot corrected the drift as the plane wobbled, yet the landing was smooth.
Every morning you should stretch on a mat for an hour.
Your kids played soccer in the garden until it got dark.
The ancient text refers to the deity by many different names.
Fighting continued along the coast last month, according to papers in Tokyo.
neighbours.notes: Step-out feeder of bonsai1/L3/N2972- (katakana ヨ), chosen as the top MLP feeder by resident attribution because play step ran out of GPU memory, so no ablation drop was measured. Test sentences written blind by a second author who saw only the label. Words the tokenizer splits into a bare ' y'/' Y' piece (yawn, yanked, Yves) read weaker (0.13-0.27) in probes.

predictions: Most fire sentences 0.3-0.6; near misses below 0.15 (you/year/yet ~0.04-0.13).
